scene_context.physical_setting: Casual dining restaurant (diner) with wooden chairs and booths.
scene_context.social_context: Public social setting witnessing a private family breakdown followed by stranger intervention.
scene_context.emotional_atmosphere: High distress, shifting to empathetic comfort, then confrontational tension.

characters.physical_description: Young boy, brown hair, glasses, plaid shirt.

initial_state.body_language_summary: Slumped shoulders, head turning between parents, eventual face-covering.
initial_state.apparent_goal: Understand the situation / Maintain family unit.

final_state.body_language_summary: Head down, hands covering face, passive acceptance of comfort.

characters.physical_description: Adult male, muscular build, short hair, beard, green long-sleeve shirt.

initial_state.body_language_summary: Leaning in, open posture, soft facial features directed at child.
behavioral_evidence: Leans down to child's eye level

final_state.body_language_summary: Tense jaw, direct stare at mother, protective stance over child.

behavioral_evidence: Shift from ignoring parents to confronting them
Physical positioning between child and environment

characters.physical_description: Adult female, red hair, sunglasses on head, leopard print scarf.

initial_state.body_language_summary: Hands covering mouth/face, wide eyes, rocking.

behavioral_evidence: Blaming child ('It kind of is his fault')
Telling child 'we don't have a family anymore'

characters.physical_description: Adult female, black beanie, dark jacket.

final_state.apparent_goal: Defend the child / Shame the mother.

desire_motivation_analysis.reasoning_chain: Child is presented with information (divorce) that threatens his social unit. His immediate reaction is to query the status of the group ('What about our family?'). This indicates a desire to maintain the existing social structure.

supporting_evidence.description: Asking 'What about our family?' with furrowed brows.

alternative_interpretations.reasoning: The loss of family structure is a threat to basic safety/security for a child.
alternative_interpretations.why_not_primary: The verbal content specifically references the 'family' unit (social), making connection maintenance the more precise proximal desire.

desire_motivation_analysis.reasoning_chain: Subject observes distress in a vulnerable individual (child). He initiates an approach behavior, lowers his physical profile to match the child, and provides verbal reassurance ('It's not your fault'). This sequence indicates an altruistic motivation to regulate the child's negative emotion.

supporting_evidence.description: Leaning in close to the child, ignoring the adults.

desire_motivation_analysis.reasoning_chain: When confronted with the child's distress and the stranger's judgment, the subject attempts to protect her own ego/self-concept by shifting responsibility to the child. This is a defensive desire to avoid guilt or negative evaluation.

supporting_evidence.description: Stating 'Well it kind of is his fault' in response to the child's self-blame.

alternative_interpretations.reasoning: She may genuinely believe this is true.
alternative_interpretations.why_not_primary: The context (adult blaming a child for an affair) strongly suggests psychological defense (rationalization) rather than objective fact-stating.

trigger_event.description: Mother says 'It kind of is his fault'.

behavioral_markers.description: Snaps head from child to mother.

desire_transitions.visual_marker_of_change: The moment his head snaps up from the child to look directly at the mother with a hardened expression.
desire_transitions.psychological_interpretation: The mother's violation of the 'caregiving' social contract (blaming the child) triggers a shift in the man from compassionate support (directed at child) to aggressive protection/moral enforcement (directed at mother).

trigger_event.description: Stranger begins speaking softly to him.

behavioral_markers.description: Stops looking at parents, lowers head, listens to stranger.

desire_transitions.visual_marker_of_change: When the child stops frantically looking between parents and lowers his gaze, focusing attention on the man's voice.
desire_transitions.psychological_interpretation: The child realizes the family dissolution is inevitable (belief update) and shifts from trying to save the family to accepting external regulation of his distress.

behavioral_sequence.behavior_description: Hands pressed firmly over mouth and nose, rocking slightly.
behavioral_sequence.inferred_mental_state: Overwhelming distress / Attempt to contain vocalization.

behavioral_sequence.behavior_description: Moves from background to foreground, enters the family's personal space, lowers body elevation.
behavioral_sequence.inferred_mental_state: Intention to intervene and connect on the child's level.

behavioral_sequence.behavior_description: Pointing index finger directly at woman_leopard_scarf while leaning forward.

key_segments_for_qa.segment_description: The mother blames the child ('It kind of is his fault') and the interveners react.
key_segments_for_qa.psychological_significance: High-value segment for Theory of Mind. The mother's statement violates standard caregiving expectations, triggering a rapid shift in the interveners' mental states from compassion to moral outrage.

inter_character_dynamics.mutual_influence: The man regulates the child's emotional state; the child's vulnerability reinforces the man's protective behavior.

key_interaction_moments.description: Man enters child's space to comfort.
Man shares personal history to build rapport.

inter_character_dynamics.mutual_influence: The woman's blame of the child triggers the man's aggression.

key_interaction_moments.description: Man snaps at woman after she blames the child.

annotation_metadata.annotation_notes: The video depicts a staged social experiment (implied by the dramatic nature and camera angles), but annotation treats behavior as genuine per instructions. The mother's behavior at 00:38 is a critical ToM violation.
